presentation: A 63-year-old man with hypertension and CAD underwent CABG two months ago and developed postoperative delirium. Today, despite orientation to person, place, and time and a normal neurologic exam in clinic, he continues to endorse intermittent confusion, delusions, and paranoid thinking. A noncontrast head CT on last month showed no acute infarct. Laboratory studies show a hemoglobin of 13.2 g/dL and hematocrit of 39%. The patient has no prior history of dementia or psychiatric illness. What is the next best step to evaluate this persistent cognitive deficit?
